alignments.note: Participle rendered as a finite-flavoured predicate; *being* is its helper under rules 7 and 9, and the lexical *confident* heads the unit under rule 17.

*of* is the complement helper introducing the accusative object phrase and attaches to its first element, as *of the fulness* keeps *of* with the determiner under rule 21. Attaching *of* to the noun *thing* instead remains defensible.
The intensive pronoun is expanded with the generic noun *thing*; rule 17 heads such a unit on the intensive word itself.
Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun *he* only, and leaves the relativizer to the participle.
The supplied relativizer *who* is the participle's helper under rules 7 and 32; the head is the lexical verb.
The indefinite article is the noun's English helper under rule 7; *good* stays separate, so no unrelated word is absorbed (rule 15).

Future indicative takes its auxiliary and its supplied object pronoun as helpers under rule 7; head is the lexical verb, not the auxiliary (rule 17). Treating *it* as `added` remains defensible, but rule 7 forbids marking a licensed pronoun `added` mechanically.
Anarthrous Greek noun; the supplied English *the* is its helper rather than the realization of any article.
Genitive noun rendered *of + noun*: rule 17 heads on the noun, and the names are split rather than sharing one head.
